A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-patching study, with the same title, authors, and original experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection cover the main text and all appendices, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation-patching experiments, translation probabilities, and confidence intervals across several models, including Patchscope and randomized-prompt controls in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds definition-generation evaluations, additional translation language-pair results, and Gemma 2 2B experiments.

M1.justification: Section 6 adapts patching to autoregressive definition generation: definition prompts can supply and receive concept latents, and the patched model generates a description. The underlying residual-stream replacement and averaging mechanism remains unchanged. TPcollect primarily clarifies the existing translation extraction procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds multi-token definition generation and corresponding BabelNet definition data for Basic English picturable concepts, substantially extending v1's word-level translation and probing coverage. Figure 10 also adds four distinct translation target-pair scenarios: German–French, English–Finnish, Finnish–Italian, and Korean–Dutch.

E2.justification: The new definition evaluations introduce Prompting, Word Patching, and Repeat Word comparisons, visibly evaluated alongside single-source and multisource latent patching in Figures 6 and 13. These substantially expand the comparator set beyond v1's translation and diagnostic controls, which remain present.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a generation-evaluation protocol using all-layer patching, semantic similarity to reference-definition embeddings, and a reference-definition loss check. Figure 6 evaluates 61 English, 38 Chinese, and 29 French concepts for Llama 2 7B. Gemma 2 2B is also added as a tested model configuration. The original 200-pair translation protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Figures 6 and 13 add controlled comparisons of single versus averaged sources and translation versus definition source contexts, including similarity to unrelated concepts. Figure 14 adds an alternative loss-based check. Together these substantially extend analysis of source-task dependence and representation usability; the existing Patchscope, randomized-prompt, and context-averaging analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and 95% Gaussian confidence intervals across evaluated examples. The new results generally follow this existing practice; v3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed reporting, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds definition-similarity and reference-loss results in Figures 6, 13, and 14, additional translation results in Figure 10, and Gemma results in Figure 12. For example, multisource-definition patching exceeds Word Patching in mean similarity in all three Figure 6 language panels. The matched original translation and appendix-control curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The residual-stream equation, language/concept subspace decomposition, H1/H2 assumptions, and averaging argument are retained. The new prompt notation and generation-patching equation instantiate the existing mathematical construction; no substantive new theoretical result, derivation, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 retains the claims about language/concept separation and multilingual averaging in translation, but adds an abstract claim and fifth contribution asserting that averaged latents support multi-token natural-language definitions. This substantially broadens the claimed usefulness of the representations beyond the original next-token translation evidence.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 newly interprets comparable translation-source and definition-source performance as evidence for representations shared across tasks. The limitations replace the translation/word-only restriction with concerns about complex and language-specific concepts, while retaining possible subtle entanglement. Appendix C.3 also explains the alternative metric as more syntax-sensitive.

D1.justification: v3 documents the definition-data construction recipe, identifies the sentence-transformers evaluation checkpoint, and explains exclusion of the selected reference definition from its comparison centroid. It also replaces the GitHub reproduction link with an anonymous code-hosting link. These are additional documentation and access instructions, without evidence of changed underlying translation settings.

R1.justification: A substantial new Related Work section expands positioning around multilingual representations, cross-lingual tuning, language-specific neurons, and causal interventions. New discussions include Choenni and Shutova, Meng et al., and Wu et al.'s semantic hub hypothesis. This replaces much of v1's generic mechanistic-interpretability framing with a focused account of the research gap.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around multilingual representation questions, a dedicated Related Work section is inserted, and Background is reorganized with an explicit activation-patching explanation. The new generation section and Appendix C.3 further restructure the narrative, although much of the original experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 removes v1's two hypothesis schematics, adds a definition-patching diagram and language/definition/loss plots, and reorganizes v1 Figure 10 into Figures 11–12 with a Gemma row. Figure 1 corrects swapped Chinese caption labels. New Figure 10 unnecessarily displays three of its four distinct scenarios twice.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's explicit restriction to word-level translation evidence by testing whether averaged latents support complete definitions, with source-task comparisons, word-based baselines, and additional model/language checks. This provides broader evidence of semantic usability, while the focused related work and revised limitations improve context. Automatic similarity scores and simple concepts still limit the conclusions; removed hypothesis diagrams and duplicated Figure 10 panels are smaller presentation drawbacks.
